question: What is the primary target group for school health inspections?
explanation: School health services are specifically designed to monitor and protect the health and well-being of children attending educational institutions. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why are schools used as strategic centers for health interventions in Nigeria?

options.A: Schools have more medical doctors than local hospitals
options.B: Parents refuse to bring children to regular health clinics
options.C: Teaching health is legally required to replace clinical care
options.D: They gather a large portion of the young population in one place

explanation: Because children spend many hours gathered in schools, it provides an efficient platform to reach a large community of young people at once. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of school health inspections?

options.A: Prescribing major surgical operations for students
options.B: Controlling the spread of communicable diseases

explanation: School inspections focus on screening, prevention, and basic health promotion, not major surgical procedures which belong in hospitals. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h2)

question: A community health nurse finds several pupils scratching itchy patches on their scalps during a morning assembly. Which school health objective does addressing this directly support?
explanation: Managing skin conditions like ringworm or lice promptly in school stops them from spreading to other children, fulfilling disease prevention goals. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h2)

question: Who usually performs the quick daily morning hygiene inspections in schools?
explanation: Daily quick checks are practical tasks often delegated to trained teachers or student health prefects under professional guidance. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the main difference between daily inspections and periodic comprehensive inspections?

options.A: Daily checks are only done by medical doctors, while periodic checks are done by students
options.B: Periodic checks ignore environmental factors completely
options.C: Daily checks focus on personal hygiene and acute signs, while periodic checks evaluate the wider school environment and deep health status
options.D: Periodic checks are done every morning, while daily checks are done once a year

explanation: Daily inspections are rapid spot-checks on individuals, whereas periodic comprehensive assessments evaluate environmental sanitation and thorough health screening. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which tool is standardly used during school physical screenings to check a child's visual acuity?
explanation: The Snellen chart features rows of letters or symbols and is the standard tool used to test distance vision in school-age children. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why are height and weight measurements routinely taken during school physical screenings?

options.A: To plot growth charts and identify malnutrition like stunting or wasting
options.B: To measure how fast a child's brain is developing academically
options.C: To determine which children are qualified to join school sports teams only
options.D: To calculate the exact daily school fee each parent should pay

explanation: Anthropometric measurements track physical growth over time, helping nurses spot signs of chronic malnutrition or nutritional excess early. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which symptom is most commonly associated with intestinal worm infestation (helminthiasis) in school children?
explanation: Intestinal parasites like hookworms rob the body of nutrients and blood, frequently leading to abdominal discomfort and iron-deficiency anemia. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h5)

question: A primary three pupil frequently squints when looking at the chalkboard and complains of afternoon headaches. What screening finding is most likely present?
explanation: Squinting at distance objects and tension headaches are classic warning signs that a child may have a refractive error requiring corrective lenses. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is a primary duty of the nurse during school health programs?

options.A: Training teachers to spot early signs of illness
options.B: Rewriting the national school curriculum for mathematics
options.C: Constructing new borehole water systems for the school
options.D: Managing the financial budget of the school board

explanation: Nurses empower school staff by training teachers to conduct daily observations and recognize when a child needs professional health attention. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h6)

question: How do midwives and community health nurses bridge the gap in child health?

options.A: By connecting families, schools, and primary health care clinics
options.B: By building private hospitals inside every school compound
options.C: By replacing classroom teachers during school hours permanently
options.D: By forbidding parents from visiting the school premises

explanation: The nurse serves as the bridge, ensuring health findings from school screenings reach parents and are followed up at local health facilities. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h6)

question: What document should be used when sending a student with a detected health defect to a higher health facility?
explanation: A formal referral slip communicates the nurse's findings and clinical suspicions directly to the receiving healthcare providers at the clinic or hospital. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why is maintaining a cumulative health card for each pupil important throughout their schooling?

options.A: It serves as a permanent report card for academic grades in mathematics
options.B: It replaces the need to ever conduct physical examinations again
options.C: It proves to the government that the school is collecting tuition fees
options.D: It tracks health trends, growth, and treatments from entry to graduation

explanation: Cumulative health records provide a continuous history of a child's health and development across the school years, aiding long-term care. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h7)
